learning_outcomes.text: Students will have the ability to make informed decisions in the design and selection of machine elements.
Students will be able to apply analytical and other frameworks to the design of commonly used machine elements.

syllabus_topics: Gears: Classification; criteria based upon axles and teeth; the case of parallel axes: spur and helical gears.
The MAAG system for cutting gears; basic rack profile; involute.
Metrology: base tangent length Wk; measurement over balls on external gears.
Addendum modification; sliding; interference; imposed center distance.
Introduction to load carrying capacity of gears.
Fatigue design: Uniaxial and biaxial loading.
Stress concentration. The improvement of fatigue behaviour. The effect of residual stress fields.
Introduction to hydrodynamic and hydrostatic lubrication.
Elastohydrodynamic lubrication: Cheng's formulation for rolling bearings cam-follower and gears.
Power transmission screws and fastening screws.
assessment_rules: The final grade (X) is calculated as 0.5 times the grade of the 1st Test (Y) plus 0.5 times the grade of the 2nd Test (Z). A minimum grade of 8.00 is required in both Y and Z to pass; otherwise, a Second Exam covering all content is mandatory. Eligibility for exams requires at least 75% attendance in theoretical-practical classes. Special exams follow FEUP's General Evaluation Rules, where the exam grade serves as the final course classification.
